recorded: Every case passed against the original, run unchanged from a copy with Node.js 26.12.1 and nothing to install, where the programs are each level's suite, test/level1.test to test/level4.test, run as node --test test/level1.test.js, the files npm run test:1 to test:4 run, and scripts/verify-solution, run as node scripts/verify-solution.js, the script npm run test:solution runs. Each suite is checked only by whether it fails, against the starting point, whose methods have empty bodies, or succeeds, against the reference solution, never by its report, because every test runner prints its own and some fail with their own exit code. The starting point's cases leave SOLUTION out, so support/helper takes src/, and the solution's set it to 1, as verify-solution does. solution/card, solution/deck, and solution/board only export their classes, so their cases run a driver written for them: its first argument names an operation, every later argument is JSON, and it prints the result as one line of JSON. solution/card new takes the four values, builds the card with the constructor, and prints its text, exiting with a failure when the constructor throws, and formsSetWith takes three card texts, builds them with Card.parse, and prints whether the first forms a set with the other two. solution/deck full prints the texts of Deck.full(), shuffle takes a deck, given as a list of card texts or as null for new Deck(), and a list of numbers the random function returns in turn, and prints the deck's cards afterwards, and draw takes a deck and a count and prints {drawn, size}, the drawn cards and the deck's size afterwards. solution/board new, findSets, and dealUntilSet take a deck the same way and deal a Board from it: new prints {cards, deckSize}, the board's cards and the deck's size, findSets prints each set as a list of three texts, and dealUntilSet prints {cards, deckSize} after dealing. The command chose by {program}, as in case {program} in test/*) node --test {program}.js ;; solution/*) node driver.js {program} {args} ;; *) node {program}.js ;; esac. The starting point has no driver case, because what an empty body returns differs per language. Every card is compared by its text, exactly and in order.
originals: case {program} in test/*) node --test {program}.js ;; solution/*) node driver.js {program} {args} ;; *) node {program}.js ;; esac
